name: Competitive Programming
description: Contest craft on top of DSA: fast I/O, templates, stress testing, constructive and interactive problems, and contest strategy.

nodes.name: Judges & ratings
nodes.desc: Online judges, verdicts, rating systems and contest formats like ICPC and Codeforces rounds.
nodes.summary: You will be able to navigate online judges, interpret verdicts and understand rating systems and contest formats such as ICPC and Codeforces rounds.
topics: Verdicts like WA, TLE and RE

nodes.name: Your template
nodes.desc: A personal C++ template: macros, typedefs, fast I/O and multi-test loops.
nodes.summary: You will be able to set up a personal C++ contest template with useful macros, typedefs, fast I/O and a multi-test loop.

nodes.name: Fast I/O
nodes.desc: Fast input and output, buffering and avoiding slow I/O patterns.
nodes.summary: You will be able to read and write large inputs quickly by using buffered I/O and avoiding slow patterns.

nodes.name: Complexity budget
nodes.desc: Reading constraints and turning them into a target time complexity.
nodes.summary: You will be able to read problem constraints and translate them into a target time complexity that fits the time limit.

nodes.name: Edge cases & overflow
nodes.desc: Overflow, off-by-one, empty input, precision and other ways solutions fail.
nodes.summary: You will be able to anticipate overflow, off-by-one errors, empty inputs and precision problems before they cost you a verdict.

nodes.name: Debugging fast
nodes.desc: Debug macros, asserts and finding the bug under time pressure.
nodes.summary: You will be able to find bugs quickly under contest pressure using debug macros, asserts and systematic checks.
topics: Testing on sample and tiny cases

nodes.name: Stress testing
nodes.desc: Random generators, a brute force and a checker script to find failing cases.
nodes.summary: You will be able to find failing cases automatically with a random generator, a brute-force solution and a comparison script.

nodes.name: Reading problems
nodes.desc: Extracting the real question, small cases by hand and spotting known patterns.
nodes.summary: You will be able to extract the real question from a statement, work small cases by hand and spot known patterns.

nodes.name: Brute to optimal
nodes.desc: Start from brute force and remove redundant work step by step.
nodes.summary: You will be able to start from a brute-force solution and remove redundant work step by step until it meets the constraints.

nodes.name: Constructive problems
nodes.desc: Build an answer that satisfies the conditions, from small patterns to proofs.
nodes.summary: You will be able to build answers that satisfy given conditions by finding small patterns and proving they generalise.

nodes.name: Ad-hoc & observations
nodes.desc: Invariants, parity and the key observation that unlocks a problem.
nodes.summary: You will be able to find the key observation in ad-hoc problems using invariants, parity and similar reasoning.

nodes.name: Implementation-heavy
nodes.desc: Simulation and long-code problems written cleanly the first time.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write long simulation and implementation-heavy solutions cleanly and correctly on the first attempt.

nodes.name: Interactive problems
nodes.desc: Flushing output, query limits and binary-search style strategies against a judge.
nodes.summary: You will be able to solve interactive problems by flushing output, staying within query limits and using binary-search style strategies.

nodes.name: Special checkers
nodes.desc: Problems with many valid answers, special checkers and output-only tasks.
nodes.summary: You will be able to handle problems with many valid answers, special checkers and output-only tasks.

nodes.name: Offline & query tricks
nodes.desc: Sorting queries, sqrt decomposition and answering queries offline.
nodes.summary: You will be able to answer many queries efficiently by processing them offline, sorting them and using sqrt decomposition.

nodes.name: Contest math tricks
nodes.desc: Modular arithmetic, precomputed factorials and common formulas.
nodes.summary: You will be able to apply modular arithmetic, precomputed factorials and common formulas that appear in contest problems.

nodes.name: Contest strategy
nodes.desc: Problem order, time management, penalties and when to switch problems.
nodes.summary: You will be able to choose problem order, manage time and penalties and decide when to switch problems during a contest.

nodes.name: Virtual contests
nodes.desc: Simulating real contests and tracking performance over time.
nodes.summary: You will be able to simulate real contests with virtual participation and track your performance over time.

nodes.name: Upsolving
nodes.desc: Reading editorials and solving the problems you missed after each contest.
nodes.summary: You will be able to learn from each contest by reading editorials and solving the problems you missed.

nodes.name: Code library project
nodes.desc: Build and test your own library of snippets: segment tree, DSU, Dijkstra and modular math.
nodes.summary: You will build and test your own library of reusable snippets including a segment tree, DSU, Dijkstra and modular arithmetic.

nodes.name: Rating climb project
nodes.desc: Do a series of rated contests with upsolving and reach your next rating tier.
nodes.summary: You will take part in a series of rated contests, upsolve after each one and aim to reach your next rating tier.
